summary: Auric is rationing heat and shelter when an evacuation freighter arrives under fire, forcing Halev to open a berth opposed by the residents he governs.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — REFUGEE BERTH AND CIVIC DOCK — NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Closer to the heater. You've been shivering all night.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: You're cold too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: Nine thousand residents depend on this berth's heat. They signed to have it closed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: I'll answer them. What's happening at the approach?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: An unscheduled freighter's coming in with the convoy. Somebody's firing on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Who's aboard?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Verge and Shard families. Couple hundred, maybe more.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: We have no safe beds left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Open the berth. Move the sleeping families clear of the gate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: The traders will pull their support.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Then they can tell me after the ship docks.

panelPlan: Auric's market ring glows faintly beneath rationed work lights. Refugee bedding crowds shuttered stalls; longtime residents and newcomers queue for the same heater.
The Luminara Mother moves her son beside the heater despite her own cold. Wallace gives Halev the residents' petition to close the berth; the names on the petition are people Halev knows.
Jex catches a broken distress transmission: a freighter carrying Verge and Shard civilians is running alongside the supply convoy and taking fire.
Halev looks toward the approaching vessel. Dock workers stand at a locked pressure gate while residents behind him argue about their dwindling heat reserves.
Halev opens the berth while the burning freighter is still outside the port. Wallace watches the dock workers obey, uncertain whether the traders who support the government will follow.
directionInline: Anchor the decision in residents, workers, a real berth, and a visibly endangered freighter. No aphoristic last line or abstract command-room debate.

summary: On Mercy of Dawn, Richard chooses the packed passenger hold over an empty bridge; his 19-year-old son Paul moves the freighter's controls onto a repair slate as attackers cut into the hull.
settingText: EVACUATION FREIGHTER MERCY OF DAWN — PASSENGER HOLD

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Brace it together. The latch won't hold on its own.

dialogueInline.speaker: Shard Caregiver
dialogueInline.text: Give that mask to the child.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: You're still short of air.

dialogueInline.speaker: Shard Caregiver
dialogueInline.text: She has less.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Dad, the bridge reserve is draining the hold. I can keep pressure in one section.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Bridge cameras clear?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Every compartment. Nobody up there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Move helm control to your slate and vent the bridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: I'll lose half the instruments.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Keep the ones you can use.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Pressure's holding. Something's cutting our outer skin.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Stay with the link. I'll take the breach.

panelPlan: Verge and Shard adults brace a bowing pressure door in a packed freight hold. The wounded Shard caregiver passes an oxygen mask to a Verge child rather than keep it.
Richard treats the caregiver while Paul, an adult engineering apprentice, reports through a battered communicator from an access crawl between the passenger hold and the supply spine.

Paul shows a power allocation on his repair slate: pressure can be maintained in the empty bridge or the occupied hold, not both. Richard checks the last bridge compartment on a local camera before deciding.
Paul vents the empty bridge and transfers limited helm and attitude control to his repair slate. The hold stops losing pressure, but the improvised control link now depends on the service spine.
Cutting torches flare against the passenger hull. Richard moves toward the threatened door while Paul stays at the service link so he can keep the freighter's remaining systems alive.
directionInline: Richard and Paul work in different parts of the same freighter. Paul is 19 and competent within the limits of improvised controls; establish the repair slate and service-spine link that become consequential later.

summary: Billie departs from an agreed cargo-focused interception to threaten a civilian refugee ship and pull Thunderbreak off Auric's supply convoy. Abby, her allied independent captain rather than her commanding officer, demands that Billie stop; their sister-in-arms trust begins to break.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: We agreed on cargo. The freighter and its passengers are off limits.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Billie, that's the passenger hull.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak won't leave its supply screen for cargo. It'll leave for people.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You know there are Shard families on that ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I know what Fleet let happen to ours. Now Venn gets to choose in front of everyone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Change course, Billie. That's not what we agreed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: The cargo's still ours once Thunderbreak turns.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: I hear families at the collar.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Break off before you open it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Lock us on. No one leaves until Fleet answers.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Billie, stop. I'm asking you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Gravefire, take us to that breach.

panelPlan: Ashfang watches the legitimate target, supply containers, separate from the civilian freighter. The agreed cargo-only plan is evident in the coordination between independent Shard captains.

Billie identifies Thunderbreak protecting the cargo screen and switches Ashfang's docking trajectory toward the occupied passenger hull. Tess, aboard Gravefire, sees the change and demands an explanation.
Billie names the old Fleet cordon that stranded Shard families. She argues that boarding the refugees will pull the cruiser off its authorized cargo assignment and leave Auric's supplies vulnerable.

Abby demands that Billie stop, speaking as a close ally with no formal authority over Ashfang. At the boarding collar a raider hears families through the bulkhead and hesitates; Billie deliberately orders the collar engaged.
Ashfang locks onto the freighter. Gravefire moves toward the breached hull rather than the supply containers; Abby's skiffs remain divided between the raid and the captains' separate decisions.
directionInline: Billie's goal is a deliberate diversion of Fleet protection from Auric's supplies; civilian danger is an unacceptable tactic she chooses, not a random explosion of anger. Preserve visual and institutional distinction between her force and Abby's.
Shard captains command their own ships within a confederation. Abby cannot issue binding orders to Billie; her objections are demands made of a trusted fellow captain and sister-in-arms.

summary: Dominion orders Venn to guard the supply convoy, but she knowingly turns Thunderbreak toward the boarded civilians, accepting exposure of Auric's medicine and heat.
panelPlan: Thunderbreak's repaired bridge has two simultaneous crises on one coherent tactical view: raiders threatening the refugee hull and the exposed medicine and heater convoy.

Dominion orders Venn to retain the authorized supply screen. The refugees' mixed registration and Shard docking codes give him grounds to demand caution, but the distress pictures show occupied compartments.
Tactical identifies the immediate cost: a departure leaves cargo undefended. The bridge crew hears Richard's distress message; a nearby officer notes that Dominion's order has been recorded.
Venn orders Thunderbreak toward the freighter despite the direct order, taking responsibility herself. The crew obeys at mixed speeds; this is not a ceremonial show of agreement.
The old cruiser leaves its position in the screen, takes raider fire on previously repaired plates, and exposes the convoy it was assigned to protect.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Your assignment is the supply convoy. Remain on that screen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: The freighter's transmitting civilian registries and live distress video.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: And Shard docking codes. I will not have you open a path for an attack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Turning exposes medicine and heater cargo for Auric.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Dominion's order is on the command log.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: And so is that distress call.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Do not turn Thunderbreak.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Helm, take us to Mercy of Dawn. I'll answer for the diversion.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Course laid in.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Auric, your convoy screen is gone. Pull what you can toward the port.

directionInline: Use the same tactical geometry across panels. Venn accepts competing human costs, and the record of her disobedience remains the basis of her tribunal case.

summary: Naomi prevents the Fleet rescue from resembling an armed occupation; Venn yields operational lead while retaining accountability for the mission.
settingText: VERGE ESCORT — COCKPIT / THUNDERBREAK RESCUE BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Mercy of Dawn to anyone listening. They're inside the outer hull.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: My team can launch now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Not with Fleet rifles leading. The families will think it's another boarding party.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Then give me a way in before the hold loses pressure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Our small shuttle can use their service collar. I'll keep the escort alongside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Verge shuttle first. Fleet medics follow me, rifles down.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: My officer has the boarding plan.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Your officer has never met the people behind that door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Officer, Sol leads passenger contact. You handle engineering support.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: The engineers will follow Sol's shuttle in.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Launch. Call me when you have pressure.

panelPlan: From her Verge escort, Naomi sees Fleet marines preparing to enter the freighter first as Richard's distress images show mixed frightened families.
Naomi calls Venn directly: visibly armed Fleet troops at the front will provoke resistance inside a ship losing air. Venn points out that postponing launch is equally dangerous.
Naomi's second identifies a workable alternative: a smaller Verge-marked rescue shuttle can reach the damaged docking collar while the escort remains outside to steer traffic.
Venn removes her own officer from the lead boarding position, retains Fleet medics and engineering support, and puts Naomi in charge of contact with the passengers.

Naomi boards the shuttle with medics, unraised weapons and practical rescue equipment. Her second keeps command of the Verge escort outside; Venn remains aboard Thunderbreak to coordinate the exposed convoy and rescue.
directionInline: Naomi takes civilian-contact lead, not command of Thunderbreak. Her second remains physically in the Verge escort; this geography must remain intact through the Shatterwake crossing.

summary: With one rescue shuttle remaining, Naomi evacuates children and a wounded Shard caregiver while she stays with Richard and the adults; Paul prepares to enter the service spine to preserve the freighter's controls.
settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — FRACTURED PASSENGER HOLD

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: One load. Children and a caregiver, or some of the wounded. We can't take both.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Children board first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: Not without her. She gave me her air.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: She can't get to the shuttle alone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Put her in my restraint. Carry her across.

dialogueInline.speaker: Junior Rescuer
dialogueInline.text: Then you're staying aboard.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You have the children. Fly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Dad, the ship's opening at the spine joint. My control link runs through it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Can you reach the spine before the hatch buckles?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: If I go now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Keep your suit line clipped. Call me when you're through.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Everybody left aboard: help us clear this compartment.

panelPlan: The passenger hold has split open along an internal frame. Naomi's one docked shuttle can carry the children and a handful of attendants, or a few more injured adults, not everybody.
The child who received the Shard caregiver's oxygen refuses to board without her. Richard needs the caregiver's weight carried across; there is no additional rescue seat.
Naomi gives the caregiver her own restraint and sends the junior rescuer to fly out with the children. Richard remains with immobile patients.

Paul reports that the section join is deforming and the repair slate's control link may be severed. He offers to move through the narrow service passage into the attached supply spine while it is still connected.
The shuttle departs. Naomi and Richard are left with the adults in the passenger section as Paul opens the spine access hatch. His father sees him take the slate and go.
directionInline: The shuttle visibly departs with the caregiver and children. Paul is 19, makes his own technically grounded decision, and begins his physical move into the supply spine before it separates.

summary: Tess stops one of Billie's raiders from stealing medical supplies, helps Naomi seal the freighter's breach, and clears a route for Paul into the spine before withdrawing to Gravefire.
settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — RAIDER BREACH / PASSENGER HOLD

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Leave the medicine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: Billie ordered us to strip this hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: That case is keeping people breathing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Then it's staying here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: Move.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Tess, hands where I can see them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Help me hold this plate before the air goes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Richard, get them behind the inner door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Spine hatch is bent. I can't turn the wheel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Bring your slate. I'll clear it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You just handed our supplies to Fleet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I handed their medicine back.

panelPlan: Gravefire has made a temporary docking collar beside Ashfang's damaged boarding breach. Tess reaches the passenger hold and finds a raider taking Richard's medical packs as air escapes through a failing pressure patch.
Tess orders the packs returned; the raider raises a weapon toward a patient trying to stop the theft. Tess disarms her own crew member. Naomi arrives armed but sees the rapidly worsening leak.
Naomi and Tess set aside their weapons and hold the patch together. Richard moves patients behind a pressure door; the packs stay with them.

Paul, attached to a safety line with his repair slate, reaches the service-spine hatch. Tess helps release its bent manual latch before he crosses. Richard stays in the passenger hold and hears Paul's access hatch close.

Tess withdraws through Gravefire's collar as it separates from the passenger hull to pursue the unstable supply spine. Billie sees the refusal on a boarding feed; Tess's action, not a speech, marks her break.
directionInline: Keep Paul moving only through connected compartments, Tess's return to Gravefire visible, and Naomi aboard the passenger hull. Tess protects civilians without assuming she has suddenly reconciled with Naomi or Abby.

summary: As Mercy of Dawn tears into a passenger hull and supply spine, Venn holds the civilians while the cargo is cast adrift; the eventual recovery of part of Auric's relief remains uncertain.
settingText: THUNDERBREAK — BRIDGE / AURIC CIVIC CONTROL / MERCY OF DAWN

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: The joint's gone. Tractor can hold one section.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Three hundred people on this side. The pressure's falling.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Dad, I'm sealed in the spine. Controls still answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Stay on the slate. We're in the other section.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: The spine's carrying our heat and antibiotics. Our clinics won't last without it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Cargo section is beyond tractor range in thirty seconds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Hold the passenger hull. Keep Gravefire's approach open.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: If that spine's lost, I need to ration tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I understand. I can't leave these people in the debris.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Clinics, protect the reserve stock. We don't have a delivery yet.

panelPlan: The freighter's deforming joint finally tears apart. Paul is already inside the supply spine behind its closed pressure hatch; Richard and Naomi are aboard the separate passenger hull. Both sections appear on Thunderbreak's tactical view.
Thunderbreak's tractor has enough available load capacity to stabilize only one section. The passenger hull still holds hundreds of living people and losing pressure.
From Auric, Halev identifies the detached spine's contents: North Ring's heater cartridges and the fever ward's antibiotic shipment. Both targets matter to different people.
Venn uses the only tractor lock to arrest the passenger hull. Gravefire is moving toward the unpowered spine, but no one can promise it can be recovered.

Thunderbreak drags the passenger hull away from immediate debris. The supply spine drifts toward shifting fragments with Paul aboard. Halev begins emergency rationing, not a declaration that the cargo is permanently destroyed.
directionInline: One tractor limit, two incompatible immediate targets. The supplies are endangered, not retrospectively declared destroyed. Make clear Paul is physically on the spine and Richard with the passenger patients.

summary: Jex opens the route geometry that protects his commercial advantage because the rescuers cannot coordinate a blind crossing; publishing it also compromises the safe houses attached to his network.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — VEIL MARKET BACK ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: That spine still has a chance. You know a way through.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: One. I built it for people who needed to stay off public routes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Can you send it to Gravefire?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Their channel's broken. Verge and Shard can't read the same private key out there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Then use the emergency band.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: That puts the approach to three safe houses in the open.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: The first marker isn't enough. The second turn has shear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: I can't make that choice for the people hiding there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Neither can I. But Paul has no course without it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Send every anchor fix and timing window. Open band.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: Both rescue craft have it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: I'll answer the safe houses when they're clear.

panelPlan: Jex watches the freighter's separated sections on a technical route table in the Veil Market. The Shatterwake is a hazardous realspace passage defined by shear forecasts, anchor fixes and moving debris; nothing supernatural.
Halev asks for the geometry. Jex shows that its private approach points also reveal the existence and approaches to clients' safe houses. There is no time to obtain their agreement.

Jex attempts to send Tess only the initial coordinates through private comms. The jamming and incompatible Shard/Verge channels prevent a reliable shared path; the public emergency channel is the only relay both rescue craft and Auric pilots can receive.
The route technician finds a second turn where an incomplete course will drive the spine into damaging shear. Jex chooses to release every required timing marker across the open emergency band.

Tess and the Verge escort correct their trajectories using the public data. Jex watches alarmed private clients abandon a once-exclusive approach on the route board; the consequences to the hidden network have begun.
directionInline: Public disclosure must be necessary for cross-faction coordination rather than a contrived public announcement. Preserve Jex's fear for actual hidden clients; the route is science and hard-won leverage.

summary: Naomi shepherds the passenger hull while Paul steers the detached supply spine through the Shatterwake, with Tess physically guiding the spine and Venn taking Thunderbreak on the longer outside course.
settingText: THE SHATTERWAKE — MULTI-LOCATION INTERCUT: REFUGEE PASSENGER HULL / SUPPLY SPINE / GRAVEFIRE / THUNDERBREAK

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Paul, nose toward the blue fracture.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: It keeps moving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Watch the blue edge. It's slower than the rest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Paul, eyes on the slate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: I can't see your section.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: I'm here. You keep flying.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak won't fit through.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Then go around.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Already turning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Supply spine's slipping. I'm going to push it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You'll tear Gravefire apart.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Maybe. Get Paul through.

panelPlan: Large exterior establishing view of a debris-filled, fractured moon region. The separate passenger hull is escorted by Naomi's Verge vessel piloted by her second; Paul rides the supply spine; Gravefire approaches the spine. Thunderbreak is too large for the gap. Moving fragments and measured reciprocal-field gradients define realspace navigation.

Inside the supply spine, Paul alone occupies a sealed machinery blister, tethered beside working attitude controls with his repair slate. Naomi radios from inside the passenger hull, and Tess guides him over comm from Gravefire. Neither woman is physically beside him.

Still inside the supply spine, Paul's small comm display briefly shows Richard tending patients in the separate passenger hold. The rotating fragments interrupt the video connection; Richard cannot be seen directly through a window from Paul's location.

Thunderbreak bridge, with Venn physically present and Naomi only heard on radio. Venn orders the cruiser around the outside of the narrow debris throat, maintaining protective cover without pretending the cruiser can fit inside.

Gravefire cockpit with Tess physically present. She uses carefully controlled contact thrusters to nudge the supply spine's yaw while Paul fires its own attitude jets. Naomi warns that Gravefire may be damaged, but Tess commits to the physical push.

Exterior close: the passenger hull and its Verge escort emerge through the first navigable gap while Paul and the recovered supply spine, pushed by Gravefire, pass a separate exit with damaged cargo pallets visibly venting. Thunderbreak moves around the exterior route, shielding their eventual run toward Auric.
directionInline: These dialogue entries alone control exact lettering; the panels never contain contradictory quoted alternatives. Keep physical locations explicit: Naomi stays aboard the passenger hull, her second pilots the Verge escort, Paul is aboard the supply spine, Richard remains with patients, Tess pilots Gravefire, Venn commands Thunderbreak. Cargo suffers damage even though the spine is recovered.

summary: Billie grapples the civilian supply spine with Paul inside and tries to use him to compel Tess. Abby, an independent fellow Shard captain, threatens force and rallies those captains who choose to protect civilians; others choose Billie. Their long friendship fractures.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Release the spine. There's a man inside it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Tess comes aboard Ashfang. Then I let the cargo go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You've already cut through a passenger hull. I won't send Paul into another one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Then the spine stays where I can break it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: This started as a cargo raid. You've made the civilians your target.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Every captain can hear you defending Venn.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: They can hear me defending a Shard pilot too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Last chance. Move your skiffs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Cut the grapple or I'll cut it for you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Paul, hold the attitude jets steady.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Holding. Gravefire's got my side.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: All ships, choose your formation. Keep weapons off that spine.

panelPlan: At the Shatterwake exit, Ashfang and Billie's skiffs intercept Gravefire and the rescued supply spine. A grappler bites into the spine's already damaged hull while Paul's pressure suit and repair slate remain visible through a small engineering port.

Billie calls across the open Shard channel: she will release the spine only if Tess submits to her. Tess pilots Gravefire beside the spine, unable to break the grappler without risking Paul and Auric's remaining heat.
Abby arrives with the Scythe's supporting skiffs. She demands Billie cut the grappler, making it clear she is protecting the spine's occupant, not accepting Fleet authority.

Billie orders a cutting charge armed. Abby fires across Ashfang's grappler assembly, damaging it, and the independent supporting skiff captains visibly choose sides: some hold beside Abby, others form on Billie's damaged flagship.

Tess keeps pushing the spine clear while Abby shields it. Billie retreats just beyond firing range with those who chose her; the division of Shard command has become operational and permanent for now.
directionInline: One climax, not a new rescue episode. Billie's coercion derives from the existing freighter and supply-spine geometry. The skiff split and Abby's damage to Ashfang have immediate consequences, no triumphant reunion with Tess.
The Shard split is voluntary allegiance among independent captains, not military insubordination. Preserve distinct craft command authority.

summary: Thunderbreak covers the damaged hulls against Billie's retreating skiffs; Venn takes responsibility for prioritizing the last tractor hold over an opportunity to strike Ashfang.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Two skiffs still firing. Point defense is saturated.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Defensive drones. Give the escorts a clear path.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Ashfang is crossing our firing line. I have a clean strike.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Strike power takes the tractor offline. Passenger hull drops into the debris.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Keep the tractor. Do not chase Ashfang.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Striking solution cancelled. Feeding the tractor bus.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Gravefire has the spine clear. Cargo damage reported.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Send Auric the condition report. They need an honest count.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Brace. Incoming on our patched port armor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Secure the bridge and keep pulling.

panelPlan: Thunderbreak completes its longer route around the Shatterwake and reaches the outgoing convoy path. The passenger hull remains in the cruiser tractor while Naomi's Verge escort holds course beside it.

Ashfang's supporters fire toward Gravefire and the recovering spine. Venn's bridge is damaged and functioning on redistributed power; an officer presents a firing solution on Ashfang while the tractor begins to fail.

Venn compares the firing solution with the passenger hull's trajectory. The same power bus cannot sustain a precision strike and the tractor field; the officer gives the true technical limit without being asked to make a moral declaration.

Venn orders power kept on the tractor, defensive drones toward the missiles, and no pursuit. Tess and Abby clear the spine from the threat; Billie withdraws with her faction rather than being defeated by a revenge shot.

Thunderbreak absorbs an impact on an already patched armor section. The passenger hull, damaged spine and their escorts clear the final debris and enter Auric's approach. Paul sees frost collecting inside his gloves as the spine's heaters struggle.
directionInline: Venn commands her ship instead of turning a junior officer into a student. Preserve cumulative Thunderbreak damage. The tactical end state: passenger hull secured, supply spine partially recovered but damaged, Billie withdrawn, Shards politically split.
Thunderbreak's port-bow section was scraped during the Kaldr grain raid in Issue 1; it was patched before renewed deployment and takes new damage now. Do not erase prior repair history.

summary: Auric receives survivors and a damaged partial cargo shipment, while the Luminara Mother's offer of a berth to a Shard caregiver challenges demands to segregate the arrivals.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: Shard arrivals stay behind the red barrier.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Keep the patients together. Some are helping the people beside them breathe.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: The heater pallets are damaged. People expected a whole convoy.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Count what works before we promise any of it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: She gave me her air.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Is your family still aboard?

dialogueInline.speaker: Shard Caregiver
dialogueInline.text: My sister was on the other shuttle. I haven't found her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Use half our berth until you do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: We've got another blanket.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: That room won't hold everyone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: No. The partitions still come down. Triage by need, not faction.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: This one first. Help me move it.

panelPlan: The recovered passenger hull docks under Verge supervision; Richard leads injured arrivals from a damaged collar. Farther down the quay, port crews tally partly crushed supply pallets and remove unusable heater cartridges from the recovered spine.

Auric residents demand a separate Shard processing area. Wallace tells Halev that anger has intensified because the badly needed cargo has arrived incomplete and continuing Fleet relief remains uncertain.

The wounded Shard caregiver, already brought ashore aboard Naomi's first rescue shuttle with the Verge child, waits beside Richard's newly arrived patients. A resident's faction barrier blocks her from a group searching for missing relatives.

The Luminara Mother recognizes the caregiver's earlier act and shifts one divider to offer half of her family's berth. The caregiver is still waiting for word of her sister. The boy offers his blanket.

Halev removes faction-separation barriers from the civilian berth but keeps medical triage and capacity checks in place. Some residents help; others refuse and depart. Repair crews continue counting salvage in the background.
directionInline: Make partial cargo recovery visually unmistakable: not no supplies, not full relief. Civilian choice precedes public direction. No instant collective change of heart or erasure of local opposition. The caregiver and child left together on the first rescue shuttle; do not place the caregiver back aboard the later-arriving passenger hull.

summary: Dominion seeks Fleet detention of Shard evacuees and threatens further relief; Venn rejects the order but remains responsible for Thunderbreak until an appointed relief officer takes command.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Hold any Shard evacuees still in Fleet custody. Ask Auric for separate detention of the others.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Auric is a civilian port. There are mixed households among our patients.

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: Security classification isn't a penalty.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Separating patients from their carers will make it one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Sol's rescue personnel will submit to inquiry if they come aboard a Fleet ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: They were responsible for bringing the children out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: Officer, that's not your jurisdiction.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Carry out the order and Thunderbreak remains yours.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I refuse the detention order. Record it without qualification.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Lieutenant Erin Deka will assume command of Thunderbreak once you're safely berthed. Until then, the ship remains your responsibility.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Then I'll bring her to a safe berth and hand her over intact.

panelPlan: Thunderbreak's damaged bridge runs on emergency systems. Dominion and Keating appear on the working Fleet channel while Auric receives civilians through Verge jurisdiction, beyond Fleet's unilateral police authority.

Dominion directs Venn to hold Shard refugees still in Fleet medical custody, surrender Naomi's rescuers for questioning if they enter Fleet jurisdiction, and request that Auric accept separate Shard detention.

Venn points to mixed families and the lives rescued. Keating insists security classification is ordinary Fleet policy; the bridge crew reacts uneasily because Dominion's demand would split patients and caretakers.

Dominion offers Venn continued command and scheduled relief only if she complies. She refuses on the recorded channel. She remains in charge of Thunderbreak's damaged shipboard systems until a replacement can assume responsibility.

Dominion names Lieutenant Erin Deka as the officer appointed to assume command once Thunderbreak is securely berthed and the formal handover is complete, and warns that future Fleet support is under review. Venn remains at the damaged command station, retaining shipboard command until then; some crew respect her decision and others fear it.
directionInline: Fleet may control its own medical facilities and personnel, not impose Auric-wide detention by fiat. Venn has not resigned or been relieved on this page, allowing a lawful handover later and preserving Issue 3 tribunal charges.

summary: Halev authorizes temporary refugee shelter in the Crown Ring despite contested ownership and a monitored structural fracture, accepting a real political and engineering limit rather than pretending the ring is safe.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: Those rooms aren't abandoned. Owners left goods behind and the gallery's fractured.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: How much of the ring can be isolated from the glass?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: These sensors still respond, but I wouldn't trust them alone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: The other plan separates care groups. Some patients can't be moved twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Then we use the inner rooms only.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: The traders hold the leases and financed your coalition.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Record every room. No permanent reassignment. Find the owners.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: We need a second watch on the crack and a clear route out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Put a repair crew on it. If it spreads, everyone leaves.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: The traders have already called a vote.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Get the people inside the isolated section tonight.

panelPlan: The Crown Ring has expensive empty-looking apartments, locked owners' goods and an observation window with a known fracture. Longtime residents' belongings are visible behind some doorways, preventing the space from reading as abandoned property.

Wallace explains that bonded goods and apartments belong to traders and families who have temporarily left; opening them without consent risks the coalition. Richard explains that the alternative dispersal plan would split mixed patients and carers.

Paul checks responsive but aging fracture sensors alongside an adult ring engineer. The engineer identifies rooms farthest from the cracked gallery that can be isolated behind working pressure bulkheads; additional shoring and a continuously staffed watch are required.

Halev opens only the isolated rooms under a written temporary shelter order. The glass gallery is cordoned off; repair teams erect shoring, maintain a clear evacuation route and agree to empty the ring if the measured crack advances.

Families enter the limited safe rooms with their possessions. Wallace receives word that the traders are withdrawing support; a resident watches strangers pass an apartment containing her family's things.
directionInline: Temporary emergency shelter only; no unsafe placement beside the fracture. Paul advises alongside qualified ring staff and is not single-handedly entrusted with safety. Plant property-rights and structural conflicts that continue in Issue 3.

summary: Naomi confronts Venn over the resources Auric must provide after Fleet's rescue; Venn offers limited authorized civilian rescue support without claiming the Verge's authority or eliminating its losses.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — SERVICE AIRLOCK OVERLOOKING THUNDERBREAK

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You saved the passengers. We got part of the cargo, but the damaged heaters and medicine are our problem now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: The route kept the people alive. I should have had a way to recover more freight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Your command can pull away. My crews still have to keep the ring warm.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I've got civilian rescue stores allocated to this emergency. Your crews can use them while the order stands.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: And when Dominion cancels it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: The replacement can recall Fleet personnel. I can't bind the Admiralty to more relief.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I won't accept a Fleet base as the price for borrowed supplies.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: No base. Verge controls the civilian work. You can have the rescue charts and tools, not Fleet tactical systems.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Put the limited loan in writing. Halev needs to know what disappears when you leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I'll sign what I'm authorized to provide.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I'll tell him. It won't make the shortages go away.

panelPlan: Naomi finds Venn at a service airlock with damaged Thunderbreak in view. Below, crews move incomplete cargo pallets and refugees toward the Crown Ring, where cordoned repair works are visible.

Naomi describes actual consequences: lost heater units, interrupted relief, a politically fragile berth, and the threat posed by the Shards who followed Billie. She will not accept that the rescue itself has solved any of them.

Venn listens without invoking heroism or demanding forgiveness. She identifies her remaining authority: noncombat rescue stores already designated for civilian relief, shared hazard charts, and a short emergency support shift; she cannot promise Dominion's future shipments.

Naomi refuses a permanent Fleet post or military command relationship. Venn places temporary civilian-use equipment and practical rescue data under Verge management, noting that a successor can recall Fleet personnel when command changes.
Both watch medics move among the arrivals. They have made one limited arrangement, not repaired the larger political disagreement or the shortage of shelter and future supply.
directionInline: No stock handover of weapons, no transfer of Fleet command codes, no unauthorized binding security treaty. Naomi's frustration concerns the persistent uneven burden and remains unresolved.

summary: Halev's emergency housing order provokes concrete opposition from owners and traders, while residents and refugees argue over their actual homes rather than an abstract referendum on kindness.
settingText: AURIC APPROACH — REFUGEE SERVICE TUG / SHARD COMMS

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: The traders have withdrawn their coalition votes. They won't release the bonded stores.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: That's my parents' apartment. Their things are inside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Their claim stands. The emergency order doesn't transfer ownership.

dialogueInline.speaker: Shard Caregiver
dialogueInline.text: My sister got off the other shuttle. Where do we go if the door closes?

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: You can use our kitchen. The room is still my family's.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: We'll find a place for both households. I can't promise it tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: The recovered heaters buy days, not a season. There's no replacement shipment confirmed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Then publish the count. People need to know what remains.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: You don't have the votes to continue this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: The order expires unless the council renews it. I'll answer them before it does.

panelPlan: In Auric's civic concourse, Wallace stands beside residents holding property records and traders who have suspended access to their private bonded stores. A Crown Ring owner points to a picture of her family outside the apartment now sheltering refugees.

Halev explains that occupancy is temporary and limited to isolated rooms; ownership remains with the families who hold it. A refugee caregiver asks where she and her sister should go if the order is reversed.

Wallace announces that the supporting trade bloc is withdrawing its votes and commercial assurances. A clerk begins tallying what emergency heaters and medicine Auric controls, revealing that the spine recovery bought time, not enough for the enlarged population.

One owner agrees to share access to her kitchen but will not surrender her family's room. Halev assigns a civic liaison to find a separate place for the owner when her relatives return, without making an unrealistic promise of available housing.

Halev signs a sunset-dated shelter order under public scrutiny. Wallace leaves without theatrics; the political loss is seen in the empty seats at the council table and in work crews still waiting for fuel.
directionInline: Do not turn homeowners into villains. The partial cargo recovery and future supply problem are stated consistently; the housing decision is time-limited and openly contested, establishing Issue 3's ownership and heat conflicts.

summary: Venn is formally relieved of Thunderbreak only after its damaged systems are secure; separately, Auric and Verge crews adopt a narrow civilian rescue arrangement without binding the Fleet or resolving the Shard split.
settingText: THUNDERBREAK — SECURED AURIC BERTH / AURIC CIVIC CONCOURSE

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Keating's relief order is authenticated. I have the bridge when you're ready.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Port armor's compromised. Tractor bus is running hot. Two watches need replacing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Engineering has the handover. I assume command of Thunderbreak.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Then the ship is yours. The refusal and the rescue are both in my log.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Auric directs civilian rescue. My escorts take operational lead, not Fleet security.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Shared emergency calls, dock access and a thirty-day review. No permanent Fleet base.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: My remaining skiffs can protect civilian traffic. Billie's captains don't answer to me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: They work under civilian traffic control while they're in Auric space.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: I'll tell my captains. Each one has to agree.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: I can sign for Auric. Not the Fleet, not the Shards.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: That's enough to start the work.

panelPlan: Thunderbreak is secured at a safe Auric berth. Lieutenant Erin Deka formally reports to the bridge as Keating's appointed acting commander with an authenticated relief order. Venn gives Deka a physical damage and watch handover, including the ship's patched armor, recent tractor strain and civilian relief inventory.

After Deka formally assumes command, Venn signs the transfer log and relinquishes her shipboard command authorization, not her permanent Commodore rank insignia. The crew's responses vary; no synchronized heroic salute and no impression Venn can still order Thunderbreak into combat.
At the Auric civic table, Halev and Naomi prepare a time-limited civilian rescue compact: Verge operational lead, Auric civilian oversight, mutual access for rescue craft and no permanent Fleet base.

Abby, appearing on a separate open channel from her divided Shard skiffs, offers voluntary escort help on civilian terms but refuses to sign for captains who followed Billie. No one claims that Venn or the Admiralty authorized this agreement.

Naomi and Halev authorize the limited compact. Outside, damaged Thunderbreak remains available only under its new Fleet command, while local tugs and volunteer skiffs must cover the immediate perimeter.
directionInline: Physically separate command relief from the Auric civilian compact. Erin Deka is the authenticated Fleet acting commander of Thunderbreak after the handover; Venn retains her Commodore rank but cannot command the ship after relief or sign a Fleet treaty. The compact is provisional and limited, and Abby's contribution is voluntary rather than a reconciled Shard fleet.

Halev is the elected Auric civilian leader and head of the wider Verge governing council, but this temporary compact binds only consenting parties and does not automatically bind all Verge worlds or independent Shard captains.

summary: Auric survives the night with incomplete supplies, disputed temporary shelter and a fragile civilian compact; Venn faces tribunal, Halev loses his coalition and former enemies help one another without resolving the war.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CROWN RING OBSERVATION GALLERY — MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Your fingers are still numb. No more tools this morning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: The ring watch is short of people.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: I nearly lost you in that spine, Paul. I'm asking you to eat one meal.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: I can eat and take the late shift.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: I'd prefer that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: They're flying my route without asking me now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Are the safe houses moving?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: The ones that can. I've got calls to make.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: The civilian arrangement starts today. The Fleet can still withdraw its support.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: We'll have to build the rest without them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: The tribunal has summoned me. I'll give them the complete log.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: Are we staying here?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Tonight.

panelPlan: Morning through the Crown Ring's cordoned observation glass: temporary shoring and isolated shelters, visible damage on Thunderbreak, and repair traffic around the recovered but partly emptied cargo spine.

Richard checks the cold injury to Paul's hands from the supply-spine crossing. Paul wants to help repair the monitored ring; Richard requires him to recover first. Nearby, the Luminara Mother and her son share breakfast with the Shard caregiver and her recovered sister.

Jex sees his once-private Shatterwake geometry copied among working navigators and receives messages from displaced clients. Halev is told the trade coalition has withdrawn its backing; the emergency shelter order is still posted for review.

Naomi and Halev distribute the limited civilian-rescue terms to local crews. Venn, now without command, receives formal tribunal travel instructions; her rescue was successful but has no clean institutional victory.

The boy looks from his sleeping place to the cordoned glass and asks his mother whether this is their home. She answers only for the present. Outside, workers keep repairing the place everyone is trying to share.
directionInline: Conclude with unfinished stability, not triumphant unity or a second battle. Partial cargo recovery, damaged ships, civic opposition, fractured Shard loyalty, practical care and Venn's removal remain visible. Set up Issue 3's housing dispute and tribunal without pre-solving either.
